intro: Fill this in at the site visit. Every number feeds the addition ballpark in JobTread, which prices Good, Better and Best at once. Write 0 when something does not apply; do not leave it blank. A bathroom or kitchen inside the addition also gets that room's intake sheet.
screenTitle: Does this addition need the exception track?
screenIntro: Every addition goes on to the Design & Pricing Agreement after the budget range: it has a new foundation and a roof tie-in. If any answer below is Yes, flag it for the CGM: the DPA is quoted individually and the contract carries the design-to-budget clause (proposal §3.4).
screen: Second storey over existing rooms, or the house roof must be re-framed
Slope, fill, poor soil, or the footprint is near a property line or easement
A utility is in the footprint: gas or electric meter, sewer lateral, septic or well
The electrical panel or HVAC system is too small to take the addition
The customer wants a design we have not built before (unusual roof, large spans, specialty roofing)
sections: Width along the house wall (for a detached building, the front wall), then depth out from the house. Outside faces of the new walls.
Finished floors on the new footprint.
Per storey. 8 for most rooms; 9–10 for garages.
Detached = a stand-alone building with four new walls, such as a garage.
Tick one; it is 1 and the others 0. Slab = footed slab with a stem wall. For piers, write the number of posts.
Tight access, slope or drainage that means DB brings an excavator. Most concrete subs include the digging.
Existing porch, deck, sunroom or room removed before building. 0 if none.
Detached buildings only: distance from the house panel to the new building.
1 for most additions; 2–3 with a tear-down.
From the job's Service Zone in JobTread. Zone 1 adds no travel. Extended (over 50 mi): enter 4 and flag it.
Where the permit is pulled. The estimator enters the fee.
None = 0 (detached). Simple = 1: shed or gable roof against the house. Valley = 2: cross-gable or valley into the house roof.
Squares of the house's own siding that must be replaced so the addition matches (100 SF = 1 square). 0 if it will blend.
Circle one. Brick or stone to match is priced by hand; flag it in notes.
Entry or service doors; sliding or hinged patio doors.
Overhead garage doors; interior and closet doors.
Doorways or wider openings cut into the existing house wall, each with a header.
Outlets, lights and switches. No = shell only.
Insulated, drywalled and painted. Yes for rooms and finished garages; No for a shell or three-season porch.
Flooring, trim and finished-room coordination. No for a garage, porch or shell.
Fixtures that need new drain and supply run into the addition. Fill in the bathroom or kitchen sheet for their finishes.
Extend = existing ductwork runs into the addition. New unit = mini-split or dedicated system. Tick one; it is 1.
For the estimator; not a formula input. Photograph both labels.
